runtime_identity_note: Receipt client metadata reports unknown revision and is not authoritative; its clean=false field is preserved below. Runtime commit identities are supplied by independent clean Git-worktree checks, not inferred from receipt metadata. Post-fix runtime: 564a0d2426a85dbb1dd3edfb34a07b54f7aaf3ae.
external_source_distribution: External proof sources, ELF objects, runtime images, machine configuration, logs and original receipts remain outside the public repository.
change: Exact relative ELF inputs use an existing validated package working directory when all captured source bytes agree and the existing lexer finds no directory-changing reference or native declaration. Ordinary source imports can define their ELF loaders before use. Unsupported paths retain mapped wrappers; basis preparation saves/restores only wrappers actually installed and checks the receipt transport against its identity.

profile_inventory_comparison.evidence: Static admitted loaded-source inventories matched to exact dependency content; not recipe-text comparison and not elapsed-time prediction
profile_inventory_comparison.conclusion: The ARM shelves include the ARM base; MLKEM adds only Library/isum.ml relevant to this closure. Heavy supplies the required ring/group theory and related algebra but lacks the ARM base. Compatibility alone does not establish which project imports a shelf already contains. Subsequent real heavy replays failed in ARM support imports, so its additional algebra is not evidence that it can replace the ARM shelf.

timing_scope: Measurements were taken alongside other proof work; they are individual recorded evaluation times, not a controlled comparison of profile or runtime speed. Preparation and leaf costs are separate.

heavy_state_conflicts.evidence_scope: Source inspection and ordinary recorded HOL diagnostic controls; these reduced controls do not establish whole ARM compatibility.
heavy_state_conflicts.priority_cause: Library/integer.ml applies integer overload priority. The heavy shelf already contains Library/floor.ml, so its following needs is skipped and does not restore real overload priority. The unchanged quoted arithmetic statement consequently resolves to int and REAL_ARITH rejects it.
heavy_state_conflicts.controlled_intervention: The two source byte sequences differ only by one inserted prioritize_real() declaration after the same imports. It changes the printed operand type from int to real and the same quoted statement is then proved with empty hypotheses.
heavy_state_conflicts.namespace_collision: The heavy environment also binds open_in to a topology theorem. The independent observed common/elf.ml call expects a file-opening function and fails with theorem type; restoring real priority alone does not repair this collision.

source_anchors.role: real overload priority skipped by already-loaded needs
function application of open_in observed to have theorem type

heavy_state_conflicts.conclusion: Do not treat a priority reset as whole-environment repair or recommend heavy for these ARM sources.

source_defined_loader_acceptance: Actual light-profile runs start without ARM ELF loaders. Ordinary source imports define them before the complete subtraction proof succeeds. Separately, the complete ARM base is admitted with zero discovered entrypoint theorem targets and no ELF calls; its defined loaders survive retained-basis transport and the fresh subtraction leaf passes both literal correctness probes.
